title: Evaluating what you generated
intro: Subjective, multi-dimensional, no ground truth — and you still have to ship. Here's the funnel.

steps.title: Why it's hard
steps.body:
- Quality is **subjective** — depends on the audience, the brand, the use case.
- **No single ground truth** — a creative prompt has many valid outputs.
- **Many dimensions** — fidelity, prompt adherence, aesthetics, coherence, temporal consistency.
- **Scale vs nuance** — you can't human-review every asset; pure metrics miss what matters.

steps.title: Four evaluators, ordered by cost
steps.body: Each tier filters for the next:

points.label: Metric
points.note: SigLIP (images), FVD (video): fast, deterministic, one 0→1 alignment number. Can't say WHY, can't judge beauty.

points.label: LLM judge
points.note: Gemini + rubric: multi-dimensional scores with reasoning and feedback. Medium cost, non-deterministic.

points.label: Rubric
points.note: Gecko: decompose → verify. Per-element pass/fail; the same questions across candidates makes comparison fair.

points.label: Human
points.note: Gold standard for nuance, culture, safety. Expensive; doesn't scale. Spend it last.

steps.title: The two automated stars
steps.body:
- **SigLIP** is a **dual encoder**: text and image embedded *independently* into a shared space; sigmoid similarity → 0→1. Perfect as a fast first filter. Mind the **max token limit** — score against a condensed prompt.
- **Gecko** decomposes the prompt into questions ("is there a cat?", "is it right of the flower?") and verifies each against the image — **interpretable** per-element results, images *and* video, via the Vertex Gen-AI Evaluation Service.

steps.title: The funnel, closed
steps.body:
`generate → auto-score → LLM/rubric → human → iterate` — and the insights **feed back into generation**.

> [!key] Evaluation is a continuous mechanism, not a checkpoint. The media agents in this pack move the judge *inside* the generation loop — every asset is born already evaluated.

recap:
**Evaluation is a cost-ordered funnel with feedback.**

- Hard because: subjective, no ground truth, many dimensions, scale vs nuance.
- Metric (SigLIP/FVD) → LLM judge → rubric (Gecko) → human.
- SigLIP = dual-encoder similarity; Gecko = decompose → verify.
- Insights flow back into generation — the loop never really closes.
